newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico attorney general removed from post - govt.
newsitem.headline: Mexico attorney general removed from post - govt.

text.p: Mexico's Attorney General, Antonio Lozano Gracia, has been removed from his post, the office of President Ernesto Zedillo said on Monday.
Lozano, of the opposition National Action Party, will be replaced by Jorge Madrazo Cuellar, currently head of the government's Human Rights Commission, Zedillo's office said in a statement.

"President Ernesto Zedillo disposed today a change at the head of the attorney general's office," the statement said. "President Zedillo thanked Antonio Lozano Gracia for his efforts during his period as attorney general. Subject to the ratification of the Senate, President Zedillo designated Jorge Madrazo Cuellar as attorney general."
Lozano was the only opposition member in Zedillo's cabinet and had been in the post since Dec. 1, 1994, when Zedillo took office.
Lozano has been unable to make headway in Mexico's most prominent political murder, that of ruling party presidential candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio in March 1994.
He has also been embarrassed in his efforts to clear up events surrounding the September 1994 killing of another top ruling party politician, Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu.
